items.name: Spec Compliance
items.note: All four BRIEF S5 items are built and pinned: interview step 7 with custom pick, docs/stack-profiles.md plus guide/hooks-and-pipeline/CLAUDE.md, the python guard, and the worktree integration test with separate discovery and selection assertions; the S2/S3/S4 hand-offs are applied or recorded as not done in the ADR.

items.name: Error Handling
items.note: write-project-config keeps exit 4 for bad names, degrades only the early in_progress call when the shared tree is missing and keeps exit 1 for a complete scaffold; test_runner names the real key in its exit 3 message.

items.name: Security Basics
items.note: Names still go through the resolver D3 rules; docs state the trust model and the two accepted residuals; no new shell surface beyond existing CLIs.

items.name: Test Quality
items.note: Guards have planted red and green cases (path forms, sys.exit(0), class methods) plus reverse allowlist checks; the integration test drives real subprocesses from a git worktree with distinct assertions for discovery and selection.

items.name: Performance Basics
items.note: The python guard reads about 1000 files in one cat-file process and parses each once (a few seconds).

items.name: Naming & Structure
items.note: Edits are section-local in shared docs; step-e prose 397 lines (cap 400); test_runner.py stays at 321 lines (net-zero); new tests live in new files.

items.name: Affected Boundaries
items.note: Producer (resolver CLI/loader output, project writer config) and consumers (four command loaders, skill prose) probed by the integration test and the prose snippet runner; --profile-root keeps the config write location unchanged, pinned by a test.

items.name: Test Hygiene Probe
items.note: Existing tests were extended or renamed only (the 3.8 prose-shape test rename, PROSE list additions); no test was weakened or deleted.
